cs.label: [section] Cíl předmětu a studijní výstupy:
cs.content: The course of European Union (EUA) addresses the role of this organisation within its own structures and, at the same time, from the external perspectives of politics and economy. Accordingly, the lectures have been divided into separate blocks, and each one then endeavours to clarify the origins of the European Community (EC), theoretical and paradigmatic approaches to the EC/EU, key institutions with its respective decision-making processes, and tools of selected policies of the European Union. The course shall call attention to the current trends taking place in the EU, eurozone, and relations of the EU with other regions. After completing this course, students shall better understand the basics of the European Union, and they shall be able to discuss and critically approach many topics in respect of the EU agenda. The course encourages students to become familiar with and capable of engaging with manifold cruces in the field of politics and European affairs. Since this is a sphere of swift changes, so it is indispensable to keep abreast of current issues. Therefore, all the students are advised to read, for instance, The Economist together with The Financial Times regularly, whilst other press is upon students' preference and liking.
